meta.title: Miss Nora and the Book Boat
meta.textType: functional: a biography of a person of the past, a blog post

paragraphs: Posted by May. On Monday, December twenty-first, I wrote this post in the school library. Lily is sitting next to me, and she is reading it on the screen. The facts come from a book about the river. It tells about Miss Nora, a woman of the past. She lived in the twentieth century. Her life was long, and it was full of books. Teacher Kim will read my post first.

Miss Nora was born in nineteen twelve in a small river village. Her father built boats. She went to a college for teachers, and she loved books. The village children had no library. In nineteen thirty-four, aged twenty-two, she started a book boat. She put two hundred books on a long wooden boat. The boat had shelves and a small roof. Each journey along the river took one week. Excited children waited at the river for the boat.

The boat was twelve meters long and two meters wide. In nineteen thirty-six, Miss Nora got her boat license. Then she could take the boat to the coast. She married a boat builder, and her husband helped her on the river. The children called her Miss Nora, and the name stayed. She was also a writer, and she wrote a book about the river. In nineteen sixty-eight, she stopped teaching. In two thousand five, the boat went to the museum.

Lily asked, "How long was her career?" "She taught for thirty-four years," I said. Her occupation was teacher, but she also loved the river. She had one grandchild, a girl, and the girl sometimes sailed with her. She died in nineteen ninety, aged seventy-eight. "She lived a long and busy life," said Lily.

Today the old boat is in the museum. The boat has been in the museum since two thousand five. It has been there for twenty-one years. A printed sign tells her story. I think that she was a great teacher, because she brought books to children. Who is a person of the past that you know? What would you ask Miss Nora?
text.summary: May writes a blog post about Miss Nora, a teacher of the past who took books to river villages on a boat. The post gives her dates, her work, and where her boat is today.
